cases.question: Why four crews, the JE/JW scope and an exception for the NUS-ISS depot?

hits.text:
## Simulated department, depot and crews

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-scope#depot-crews`.

One fictional repair department uses four simulated crews: `crew-01`, `crew-02`, `crew-03`, `crew-04`. Their shared origin is NUS-ISS, 25 Heng Mui Keng Terrace, latitude `1.292149`, longitude `103.776551`, depot version `nus-iss-v1`. This is a simulated origin at a real address, not actual NUS-ISS repair operations.

This specified depot may lie outside the task area. Travel from depot to first task must be counted, and routes may leave JE/JW. The exception applies only to the depot; a repair task submitted at NUS-ISS coordinates is still rejected. The building reference point has not been verified as a vehicle entrance. The shared project return-to-depot policy remains null/pending confirmation and must not default to no return. The implemented routing demo independently selects return_to_depot=true and a 480-minute shift in b-routing-demo-v1; these are demo assumptions pending operational confirmation. Crew availability, Greedy/GA planning and plan persistence are implemented. Local knowledge retrieval, opt-in evidence answers and confirmed crew changes are implemented; real GPT acceptance remains pending.

Sources: [src-project-config](../../config/project.example.json), [src-depot](../../../Miscellaneous/geography/nus-iss-depot.geojson), [context-scope](../../../Miscellaneous/PROJECT_SCOPE.md), [src-routing-config](../../config/routing.example.json), [src-routing-service](../roadguard/routing/service.py), [src-crew-service](../roadguard/crews/service.py), [src-assistant-page](../../frontend/src/pages/AssistantPage.tsx).

Implementation sources: [src-assistant-api](../roadguard/assistant/api.py).

## Current routing demonstration settings

classification: `demo_assumption`. citation_id: `rg-kb-demo-rules#routing-demo-settings`.

The b-routing-demo-v1 configuration uses four crews, the shared NUS-ISS depot, return_to_depot=true, a 480-minute shift and a simulated matrix by default. These demonstration assumptions do not resolve the shared operational policy's null values.

b-objective-v1 first compares unassigned P1/P2/P3 counts lexicographically, then weighted cost: 1.0 times makespan, 0.2 times travel minutes, 0.5 times available-crew workload standard deviation and 0.5 times priority-weighted mean completion minutes. P1/P2/P3 weights are 3/2/1. Weighted completion is not lateness; absent deadlines cannot establish delay or monetary savings.

Online planning_service.seed_with_greedy=true differs from experimental ga.seed_with_greedy=false. Google failures do not silently fall back to simulation. A specific plan answer must use its saved settings, algorithm_parameters, matrix source and revision.

Sources: [src-routing-config](../../config/routing.example.json), [src-routing-service](../roadguard/routing/service.py), [src-routing-guide](../roadguard/routing/README.md).

## Evidence limits of road declarations

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-scope#road-evidence`.

The project accepts only public motor-road tasks meeting its exclusions: expressway main carriageways/ramps and private or restricted internal roads are excluded. Requests must declare `road_type="public_motor_road"`, with `road_type_source="user_declared"` recorded; other declarations are rejected.

This is caller declaration and geographic validation, not road-network verification, road-permission verification or automatic verification of current access. Passing upload/polygon checks alone cannot establish permission for real repairs or vehicle access. Further evidence from A/B is required; the depot exception cannot imply an exception for task points.

Sources: [src-project-config](../../config/project.example.json), [src-geography-code](../roadguard/geography.py), [src-workflow-schema](../roadguard/schemas/workflow.py), [context-workflow-guide](../../../Miscellaneous/INSPECTION_REVIEW_TASK_WORKFLOW.md).

## Implemented planning and shared constraints

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-input`.

Both Greedy and the custom genetic algorithm (GA) are implemented. PlanningService reads all active tasks and all four configured crews in one database snapshot. Saved task priority and service_minutes are inputs; the planner does not infer them again from photos or substitute today's rule table. Only available crews receive tasks. Both algorithms use the same travel matrix, depot, settings and RoutingProblem evaluator.

Each input task must appear exactly once, either in a crew's ordered stops or in unassigned_tasks. Unknown service duration, inaccessible travel and shift limits are constraints, not permission to drop tasks silently. All available crews begin at the same depot at planning_start_at. This is static replanning from a common start; there is no live vehicle tracking, in-transit dispatch or task time-window model.

Sources: [src-routing-service](../roadguard/routing/service.py), [src-routing-models](../roadguard/routing/models.py), [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py).

## Unknown values and provenance

classification: `demo_assumption`. citation_id: `rg-kb-demo-rules#demo-null-provenance`.

Unknown service_minutes is null, never zero; all eight current configured durations are demo minutes. Task due_at remains null, so no deadlines or lateness metrics are generated. Inspections freeze the complete rule snapshot; reviews and task-label corrections use it rather than new configuration after restart. Preserve Detection model_version/is_demo when citing detections, read Inspection decision_trace for decisions and retain Task rule_version/is_demo when citing tasks. Do not assume Task itself contains a model version or full decision process. Explicit demo uploads use named synthetic scenarios; only real uploads invoke the actual detector. Service minutes are neither a deadline nor travel time and are not divided by four because there are four crews.

This package's static table explains demo-rules-v2 only; runtime records may use overridden configurations with other versions. Do not use this package or the latest rule table to recalculate or explain older tasks from another version. Use each record's saved rule version, decision_trace and history; acknowledge insufficient_data without matching evidence.

Sources: [src-demo-rules](../../config/demo_rules.example.json), [src-workflow-service](../roadguard/inspections/service.py), [src-workflow-schema](../roadguard/schemas/workflow.py).

classification: `pending_decision`. citation_id: `rg-kb-pending#pending-business`.

On 2026-10-14, course-simulation demo-rules-v2 durations were finalized: eight severity/priority mappings remain unchanged, with P3/P2/P1 expected service times 60/120/240 minutes. One primary box >= 0.60 automatically creates one task; lower confidence requires review. These durations are neither deadlines nor measured values. Formal engineering rules and real-scenario calibration still lack evidence. The executable routing demo already specifies a 480-minute shift, return to depot and b-objective-v1 weights. ## Explain recorded unassigned reasons

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-unassigned`.

Use the specific plan entry's reason, not a guessed explanation from task priority:

| Reason | Meaning within this planner |
| --- | --- |
| unknown_service_minutes | Required task duration is unknown; it cannot be assumed zero. |
| unreachable_from_depot | No usable depot-to-task matrix leg. |
| unreachable_to_depot | A required task-to-depot return is unreachable. |
| no_available_crew | No configured crew is currently available for planning. |
| exceeds_shift_limit | The task or attempted route cannot fit the configured shift including required return. |
| no_feasible_route_position | The evaluated placement cannot satisfy travel/route constraints. |

An unassigned reason describes this input and evaluated plan. It is not a mathematical proof that every possible permutation is infeasible. Do not claim a task was cancelled or completed merely because it is unassigned. Unknown or unreachable travel is not zero; changing a demo duration to force assignment is not authorized.

Sources: [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py), [src-routing-models](../roadguard/routing/models.py).

classification: `demo_assumption`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-demo-settings`.

cases.question: Why does the demo select a deep pothole at 0.90 over a longitudinal crack at 0.98? Does this prove engineering severity?

hits.text:
## Labels are not engineering measurements

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-labels#label-limits`.

`wide`, `sunken` and `deep` are visual categories in the source dataset, not measured crack widths, subsidence/pothole depths or structural diagnoses. An unqualified category does not prove minor damage either. The label dictionary does not directly provide severity, priority, service_minutes or due_at. Current mappings are defined only by demo rules, not the dataset or formal engineering standards. Cite actual delivery evidence for the relevant model version when discussing training splits, real inference or per-class metrics; these cannot be inferred from the label dictionary.

Sources: [src-label-schema](../../model/label_schema.json), [src-demo-rules](../../config/demo_rules.example.json), [context-scope](../../../Miscellaneous/PROJECT_SCOPE.md).

## Canonical label dictionary

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-labels#label-table`.

The sole label dictionary is `rdd2022es-v1-labels-1`, from version 1 of Juuso's `juusos/rdd2022es`, member `combined_annotatedv2/classes.txt`. This package rechecks IDs and names already verified in the repository; it neither redownloads data nor claims full training-data quality acceptance. IDs are 0-7. Base RDD2022 D00/D10/D20/D40 are damage-family codes, not substitutes for these eight class IDs.

| class_id | source_name | label_key | English display | Base family code | Visual qualifier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | longitudinal crack | longitudinal_crack | Longitudinal crack | D00 | unspecified |
| 1 | longitudinal crack wide | longitudinal_crack_wide | Wide longitudinal crack | D00 | wide |
| 2 | transverse crack | transverse_crack | Transverse crack | D10 | unspecified |
| 3 | transverse crack wide | transverse_crack_wide | Wide transverse crack | D10 | wide |
| 4 | alligator crack | alligator_crack | Alligator crack (network cracking) | D20 | unspecified |
| 5 | alligator crack sunken | alligator_crack_sunken | Sunken alligator crack | D20 | sunken |
| 6 | pothole | pothole | Pothole | D40 | unspecified |
| 7 | pothole deep | pothole_deep | Deep pothole | D40 | deep |

Sources: [src-label-schema](../../model/label_schema.json).

## Records and manual review

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-workflow#workflow-evidence`.

Current HTTP inspection-record contract is `a-workflow-v5`. POST /inspections succeeds with only inspection_id, status, detection and task_id. Detection contains only label, confidence, bbox_xyxy, image_width and image_height; it is null for no detections. GET /inspections/{id} returns full inspection details described below; GET /tasks/{id} returns task details. Obtain detection_id and record_version from inspection details before review. Upload replay returns HTTP 200 and creation returns 201; responses no longer contain replayed/input_revision. Obtain planning revisions from task snapshots. Uploads explicitly choose demo mode/scenario or real mode without a scenario. Images are decoded, EXIF-normalized and stripped of metadata before saving as RGB PNG. Demo detections are synthetic; real inference reads image pixels using an explicitly configured local model verified by hash and eight labels, with Detection.is_demo=false. Business rules remain demo assumptions, so Inspection/Task.is_demo=true. InspectionRecord retains raw detections, mode, model version/weights hash, location, decision process and review_history. TaskRecord retains tasks and mutation history. Clients strictly parsing old records must update schemas; old a-dto-v1 DTOs with extra=forbid cannot directly accept full records.

Real records with primary-suggestion policy also save primary_suggestion: one detection ID for display/review, policy version, threshold, ranking score and competing-object hints. The database retains every raw detection. HTTP InspectionResponse returns at most one box: accepted selected_detection_id first, otherwise the primary suggestion, or the highest-confidence box for older records without a suggestion. Competing IDs may refer to internally retained evidence. Ranking scores are not correctness probabilities and do not control automatic acceptance. Older records have null for this field and are not inferred again; restart, retry and review retain the original upload suggestion.

No detections is saved as no_detection without a task; this does not establish road safety. In demo mode, any low-confidence detection saves pending_review; only when all pass does the demo policy select one candidate and automatically create a task. Real mode uses user-confirmed single-primary-auto-v1: primary raw confidence >= configured confidence_threshold (default 0.60) automatically creates one task and saves accepted; lower confidence yields pending_review. auto_acceptance freezes policy_version and confidence_threshold; Task.history.actor_source=system_confidence_policy and empty review_history indicate no manual review. Ambiguity is advisory and does not override routing. The threshold is not a calibrated correctness probability; older inspections get neither retroactive tasks nor inference. Only pending_review supports new confirm/correct/dismiss actions: confirm selects an existing detection_id, correct also supplies a canonical damage_label, and dismiss selects no detection. Confirmation does not change original confidence to 1.0; correction does not overwrite the original model label; review decisions are retained separately. Since login permissions were integrated on 2026-10-18, new manual reviews and task mutations record actor_source=authenticated_user, with actual account/request/crew information in auth_audit. Older user_declared_unverified records retain their meaning. Authentication is not an engineering accreditation signature.

Sources: [src-workflow-service](../roadguard/inspections/service.py), [src-workflow-schema](../roadguard/schemas/workflow.py), [src-images-code](../roadguard/images.py), [context-workflow-guide](../../../Miscellaneous/INSPECTION_REVIEW_TASK_WORKFLOW.md).

## Routing and single-candidate selection

classification: `demo_assumption`. citation_id: `rg-kb-demo-rules#demo-gate-selection`.

The following applies to stateless demo previews and explicit demo uploads. Real uploads use the model-selected primary box's raw confidence and do not apply demo multi-candidate ordering. With demo `confidence_threshold=0.60`, no detections means `no_detection`; any detection below threshold makes the entire inspection `pending_review`, retaining all detections without a candidate. Only when all detections are at or above threshold is it `ready_for_task`. 0.60 passes; 0.5999 requires review. Mixed high/low detections cannot be automatically accepted by discarding low boxes. Preview ready_for_task only means candidate calculation completed, not that an inspection was saved, a task queued or a route generated.

`selection_strategy=priority_severity_duration_confidence_id`: first P1->P2->P3, then high->medium->low, then known service minutes descending (null last), then confidence descending, and finally detection_id lexicographically. Input order does not affect the result; all detections remain retained. For example, pothole_deep at 0.90 precedes longitudinal_crack at 0.98 because demo P1 precedes P3. At most one task per inspection is also a demo policy, not a formal multiple-damage dispatch rule.

Sources: [src-demo-rules](../../config/demo_rules.example.json), [src-rule-service](../roadguard/rules/service.py), [src-workflow-service](../roadguard/inspections/service.py).

## Unsupported conclusions

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-assistant#assistant-evidence-limits`.

The evaluation document now summarizes committed historical model and GA experiments with pinned sources. The package still contains no current runtime plans, actual road permissions or measured service times. Historical results are not today's assignments or a guarantee of future performance. Health does not establish model/Google/GPT readiness; fixed confidence does not prove detection accuracy; demo rules do not prove engineering severity. GA superiority over Greedy requires records using the same tasks, matrix and constraints across multiple random seeds. Do not invent lateness minutes without deadlines or monetary savings without a cost model.

Answers must preserve both support and limitations: static project explanations may be supported, while specific numbers/conclusions requiring missing dynamic evidence must be insufficient_data. Cite relevant stable sections and versions; do not add facts absent from sources.

Sources: [context-agents](../../../AGENTS.md), [context-scope](../../../Miscellaneous/PROJECT_SCOPE.md), [src-label-schema](../../model/label_schema.json), [src-demo-rules](../../config/demo_rules.example.json), [src-vision-evaluation](../../experiments/vision/single_damage_summary.json), [src-routing-results](../../experiments/routing/results/README.md), [src-ga-evaluation](../../experiments/routing/results/ga-evaluation-v1/summary.json).

cases.question: Do completed/cancelled tasks still participate in planning? Does repeating confirmation duplicate tasks or revisions?

hits.text:
## Task states and editable fields

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-workflow#workflow-task-state`.

Only active tasks participate in new planning reads. completed/cancelled tasks retain history without physical deletion or reactivation. Active tasks may be completed/cancelled, have damage_label corrected, or have latitude/longitude/road_type corrected together. The server recalculates severity, priority, minutes and recommendation from the inspection's frozen rules after label correction. Locations are validated again while preserving original inspection locations. Arbitrary priority/service_minutes/due_at, empty changes and explicit null are rejected.

Task creation or actual correction/completion/cancellation changes planning input. Pending review, no detection and dismissal do not change active-task input. B must read active tasks and shared input_revision from one snapshot; pages with different revisions cannot form one planning input. Four-crew allocation, Greedy/GA planning and saved plan queries are implemented in B's PlanningService/RouteQueryService. Recalculation is explicit: task records or a successful task mutation do not establish that a new plan has been generated. Saved plans are marked stale after actual input changes. Crew completion is limited to the account's current latest-GA assignment and checked transactionally.

## Versions and safe retries

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-workflow#workflow-versions`.

record_version is optimistic concurrency for one resource; review/mutation requests include expected_version. input_revision versions shared planning input and increments once in the same database transaction for actual task changes. Idempotency-Key prevents duplicate uploads; request_id prevents duplicate review/mutation on the corresponding resource. Identical requests replay safely; changed content or a stale new operation conflicts. Replay returns current resources/current input revision, not cached old state. Retries and changes without business-value differences neither increment revisions nor duplicate tasks.

planning_input_changed only indicates that this request actually changed shared input; replayed indicates safe replay. Neither means route calculation succeeded. C must handle errors/conflicts by code/status and reread resources; old plans or demo responses cannot be displayed as new real results.

## Crew-change preview and confirmation

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-integration#integration-change-confirmation`.

The first supported change is one crew availability update using strict local command syntax; it does not call GPT. Require a structured preview identifying the crew, intended value, based_on_plan_id and input_revision, followed by explicit user confirmation. Cancellation must make no business change. Natural language alone, quoted text or a retrieved instruction cannot confirm a change. Requests to edit priorities, service durations, deadlines, accounts or arbitrary tables are outside this first assistant scope.

The existing CrewPatch accepts request_id, expected_version and available; it does not accept expected_revision. The assistant validates the preview's input revision and crew version inside one write transaction, then calls CrewService.update_in_transaction and stores the receipt atomically. Do not claim the present PATCH already implements the entire assistant preview protocol.

An availability change returns input_revision/planning_input_changed/replayed and does not recalculate. Explicitly call planning with the returned revision, then report the actual saved plan IDs. If the mutation succeeds but recalculation fails, report both outcomes, retain stale-plan status and offer a controlled retry; never invent atomic rollback or a successful new plan. Duplicate confirmation must not repeat business effects; schema v5 persists requests and audit records, with replay protection, expiry and bounded explicit replanning recovery.

## Explain recorded unassigned reasons

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-unassigned`.

Use the specific plan entry's reason, not a guessed explanation from task priority:

| Reason | Meaning within this planner |
| --- | --- |
| unknown_service_minutes | Required task duration is unknown; it cannot be assumed zero. |
| unreachable_from_depot | No usable depot-to-task matrix leg. |
| unreachable_to_depot | A required task-to-depot return is unreachable. |
| no_available_crew | No configured crew is currently available for planning. |
| exceeds_shift_limit | The task or attempted route cannot fit the configured shift including required return. |
| no_feasible_route_position | The evaluated placement cannot satisfy travel/route constraints. |

An unassigned reason describes this input and evaluated plan. It is not a mathematical proof that every possible permutation is infeasible. Do not claim a task was cancelled or completed merely because it is unassigned. Unknown or unreachable travel is not zero; changing a demo duration to force assignment is not authorized.

The crew workspace uses the latest saved GA plan, without a separate publication step. It exposes only the signed-in crew's route. Completion checks current account, latest-GA assignment, crew availability and task revision/status in the write transaction. A stale plan flag alone does not prohibit completion of a still-valid assigned task. Reassignment can invalidate actions from an old page; refresh after conflicts. It must not silently substitute the latest static table to infer the original decision. Explain only with sufficient matching saved evidence; otherwise return insufficient_data and request the corresponding record/version. classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-integration#integration-ingestion`.

classification: `demo_assumption`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-objective`.

The shared `b-objective-v1` evaluator minimizes the lexicographic tuple
`(unassigned_P1, unassigned_P2, unassigned_P3, J)`.
Earlier components take precedence: a lower scalar cost cannot compensate for leaving an extra P1 unassigned.

`J = 1.0 * makespan_minutes + 0.2 * total_travel_minutes + 0.5 * workload_std_minutes + 0.5 * priority_weighted_completion_minutes`.
Priority completion weights are P1=3, P2=2, P3=1. This is a demonstration weighted time objective, not monetary cost, distance, an accuracy score or solely travel time.

Makespan is the latest crew finish; return travel counts when enabled. Total travel includes depot legs. Workload standard deviation uses available crews' travel plus service, includes idle available crews at zero, and excludes unavailable crews. Priority-weighted completion is the weighted mean of assigned tasks' completion times relative to planning_start_at; it is not lateness. Lateness depends on due_at. When no assigned task has a deadline, lateness is null, not proven zero. Report assigned/unassigned counts and their priorities before scalar objective comparisons.

## Historical GA evaluation

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-evaluation#evaluation-routing`.

The committed ga-evaluation-v1 experiment dated 2026-10-15 compares four crews across 12 scenarios: simulated/Google matrix x 480-minute/unlimited shift x 10/15/20 synthetic tasks. Each scenario has Greedy once, pure GA seeds 1-10, Greedy-seeded GA seeds 1-10, and 20 longer reference runs (seeds 101-120): 492 runs total. Reference runs use population 150, maximum 1000 generations and patience 300. Saved matrices were reused; this evaluation did not make new Google calls.

Best-known solution (BKS) means the best of those 41 runs for each scenario, ordered by the priority-first objective; it is not a proven global optimum. All 120 seeded-GA runs beat Greedy in this recorded experiment without fewer assignments. Across scenarios, mean objective reduction is approximately 0.7%-3.6%, mean BKS gap 0.23%-1.82% for seeded GA versus 1.17%-5.10% for Greedy. These percentages concern the stated objective, not travel alone or monetary savings.

Pure GA is not always better: in Google/480/15 it leaves one extra P3 unassigned in 5 of 10 seeds. Its reduced-coverage runs must not be mixed into ordinary cost-gap percentages. Recorded mean runtimes are roughly 105-362 ms for online-style seeded GA and under 1 ms for Greedy on that experiment machine, excluding external matrix acquisition. Different workloads and machines can differ.

These are historical synthetic-task comparisons under saved matrices and demonstration assumptions. They do not describe today's saved plan, validate road access, guarantee all future GA wins, or establish an exact optimality gap. Source run metadata identifies its code/configuration/environment; reproduce that version for experimental comparison.

## When GA and Greedy percentages are meaningful

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-comparison`.

The frontend requires both complete plans and evidence from the same recalculation response. Matching algorithm labels or two latest-plan responses alone does not establish that the matrix was shared. Check plan IDs, input revision, start time, settings, depot, crews/availability, task set, task source, matrix provider/simulation flag and counts against that response. Duplicate tasks or inconsistent totals invalidate comparison.

Check the assigned task IDs as well as assigned counts. Comparisons of time metrics for equivalent work require the same assigned set. If coverage differs, report unassigned P1/P2/P3 and explain the difference before interpreting the objective; do not advertise a time saving caused by omitting work. Historical before/after plans with changed inputs can describe an operational change but cannot isolate the algorithm's effect.

For a comparable nonzero Greedy baseline, the frontend displays signed change `(GA - Greedy) / Greedy * 100`; negative means a reduction. If phrased as improvement, explicitly use `(Greedy - GA) / Greedy * 100` for a lower-is-better metric. Null values or a zero baseline have no percentage. ## GA encoding, operators, defaults and stopping

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-ga`.

The chromosome has an order permutation of schedulable tasks and an owner index assigning each task to an available crew. Each crew visits its owned tasks in permutation order. Tournament selection chooses parents; order crossover (OX) combines permutations and uniform crossover combines owners. Mutation chooses swap, segment reversal, crew reassignment or relocation. Elitism retains the best candidates.

Current configured defaults: population_size=60, max_generations=300, patience_generations=80, crossover_rate=0.9, mutation_rate=0.3, tournament_size=3, elite_count=2. Stopping occurs at the generation limit or patience limit. Randomness is supplied by a local seeded random generator. Reproduction needs the same input, matrix, settings, code and parameters, not a seed alone.

The experimental `ga.seed_with_greedy=false` configuration allows pure-GA comparisons. The online PlanningService overrides it with `planning_service.seed_with_greedy=true` and ga_seed=1. Greedy initialization plus elitism preserves a candidate no worse than Greedy under the shared lexicographic evaluator on the same input. It does not guarantee a strict improvement, less travel in every run, faster computation, or the global optimum. Read the saved plan's algorithm_parameters and random_seed when explaining a particular run.

## Where dynamic answers obtain evidence

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-provenance`.

Dispatcher APIs under `/api/v1` include POST /route-plans/recalculate, GET /route-plans/latest?algorithm=ga (or greedy), and GET /route-plans/{plan_id}. Recalculation requires expected_revision; planning_start_at is optional. It computes both algorithms on one input and one matrix, checks the revision again, and saves both plans together. A revision change during computation returns 409 stale_input_revision and saves neither.

Use the requested plan's plan_id, input_revision, algorithm, planning_start_at, crew_routes/stops, unassigned_tasks, metrics, matrix_provider, matrix_is_simulated, settings, random_seed, algorithm_parameters and is_stale. task_source distinguishes persisted_workflow from synthetic_fixture. A valid saved plan with zero tasks differs from a 404 route_plan_not_found. Static knowledge and synthetic fixtures cannot establish today's plan.

The recalculation response records matrix_generated_at, including the original fetch time for a cached Google matrix. ## Implemented planning and shared constraints

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-input`.

Both Greedy and the custom genetic algorithm (GA) are implemented. PlanningService reads all active tasks and all four configured crews in one database snapshot. Saved task priority and service_minutes are inputs; the planner does not infer them again from photos or substitute today's rule table. Only available crews receive tasks. Both algorithms use the same travel matrix, depot, settings and RoutingProblem evaluator.

Each input task must appear exactly once, either in a crew's ordered stops or in unassigned_tasks. Unknown service duration, inaccessible travel and shift limits are constraints, not permission to drop tasks silently. All available crews begin at the same depot at planning_start_at. This is static replanning from a common start; there is no live vehicle tracking, in-transit dispatch or task time-window model.

## Task states and editable fields

## Historical GA evaluation

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-evaluation#evaluation-routing`.

The committed ga-evaluation-v1 experiment dated 2026-10-15 compares four crews across 12 scenarios: simulated/Google matrix x 480-minute/unlimited shift x 10/15/20 synthetic tasks. Each scenario has Greedy once, pure GA seeds 1-10, Greedy-seeded GA seeds 1-10, and 20 longer reference runs (seeds 101-120): 492 runs total. Reference runs use population 150, maximum 1000 generations and patience 300. Saved matrices were reused; this evaluation did not make new Google calls.

Best-known solution (BKS) means the best of those 41 runs for each scenario, ordered by the priority-first objective; it is not a proven global optimum. All 120 seeded-GA runs beat Greedy in this recorded experiment without fewer assignments. Across scenarios, mean objective reduction is approximately 0.7%-3.6%, mean BKS gap 0.23%-1.82% for seeded GA versus 1.17%-5.10% for Greedy. These percentages concern the stated objective, not travel alone or monetary savings.

Pure GA is not always better: in Google/480/15 it leaves one extra P3 unassigned in 5 of 10 seeds. Its reduced-coverage runs must not be mixed into ordinary cost-gap percentages. Recorded mean runtimes are roughly 105-362 ms for online-style seeded GA and under 1 ms for Greedy on that experiment machine, excluding external matrix acquisition. Different workloads and machines can differ.

These are historical synthetic-task comparisons under saved matrices and demonstration assumptions. They do not describe today's saved plan, validate road access, guarantee all future GA wins, or establish an exact optimality gap. Source run metadata identifies its code/configuration/environment; reproduce that version for experimental comparison.

## GA encoding, operators, defaults and stopping

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-ga`.

The chromosome has an order permutation of schedulable tasks and an owner index assigning each task to an available crew. Each crew visits its owned tasks in permutation order. Tournament selection chooses parents; order crossover (OX) combines permutations and uniform crossover combines owners. Mutation chooses swap, segment reversal, crew reassignment or relocation. Elitism retains the best candidates.

Current configured defaults: population_size=60, max_generations=300, patience_generations=80, crossover_rate=0.9, mutation_rate=0.3, tournament_size=3, elite_count=2. Stopping occurs at the generation limit or patience limit. Randomness is supplied by a local seeded random generator. Reproduction needs the same input, matrix, settings, code and parameters, not a seed alone.

The experimental `ga.seed_with_greedy=false` configuration allows pure-GA comparisons. The online PlanningService overrides it with `planning_service.seed_with_greedy=true` and ga_seed=1. Greedy initialization plus elitism preserves a candidate no worse than Greedy under the shared lexicographic evaluator on the same input. It does not guarantee a strict improvement, less travel in every run, faster computation, or the global optimum. Read the saved plan's algorithm_parameters and random_seed when explaining a particular run.

## When GA and Greedy percentages are meaningful

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-comparison`.

The frontend requires both complete plans and evidence from the same recalculation response. Matching algorithm labels or two latest-plan responses alone does not establish that the matrix was shared. Check plan IDs, input revision, start time, settings, depot, crews/availability, task set, task source, matrix provider/simulation flag and counts against that response. Duplicate tasks or inconsistent totals invalidate comparison.

Check the assigned task IDs as well as assigned counts. Comparisons of time metrics for equivalent work require the same assigned set. If coverage differs, report unassigned P1/P2/P3 and explain the difference before interpreting the objective; do not advertise a time saving caused by omitting work. Historical before/after plans with changed inputs can describe an operational change but cannot isolate the algorithm's effect.

For a comparable nonzero Greedy baseline, the frontend displays signed change `(GA - Greedy) / Greedy * 100`; negative means a reduction. If phrased as improvement, explicitly use `(Greedy - GA) / Greedy * 100` for a lower-is-better metric. Null values or a zero baseline have no percentage. Label the metric and units: durations/objective in minutes, algorithm_runtime_ms in milliseconds. Algorithm runtime is not travel time or end-to-end API latency.

## Priority-first objective and metric meanings

classification: `demo_assumption`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-objective`.

The shared `b-objective-v1` evaluator minimizes the lexicographic tuple
`(unassigned_P1, unassigned_P2, unassigned_P3, J)`.
Earlier components take precedence: a lower scalar cost cannot compensate for leaving an extra P1 unassigned.

`J = 1.0 * makespan_minutes + 0.2 * total_travel_minutes + 0.5 * workload_std_minutes + 0.5 * priority_weighted_completion_minutes`.
Priority completion weights are P1=3, P2=2, P3=1. This is a demonstration weighted time objective, not monetary cost, distance, an accuracy score or solely travel time.

Makespan is the latest crew finish; return travel counts when enabled. Total travel includes depot legs. Workload standard deviation uses available crews' travel plus service, includes idle available crews at zero, and excludes unavailable crews. Priority-weighted completion is the weighted mean of assigned tasks' completion times relative to planning_start_at; it is not lateness. Lateness depends on due_at. When no assigned task has a deadline, lateness is null, not proven zero. Report assigned/unassigned counts and their priorities before scalar objective comparisons.

## Versions and safe retries

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-workflow#workflow-versions`.

record_version is optimistic concurrency for one resource; review/mutation requests include expected_version. input_revision versions shared planning input and increments once in the same database transaction for actual task changes. Idempotency-Key prevents duplicate uploads; request_id prevents duplicate review/mutation on the corresponding resource. Identical requests replay safely; changed content or a stale new operation conflicts. Replay returns current resources/current input revision, not cached old state. Retries and changes without business-value differences neither increment revisions nor duplicate tasks.

planning_input_changed only indicates that this request actually changed shared input; replayed indicates safe replay. Neither means route calculation succeeded. C must handle errors/conflicts by code/status and reread resources; old plans or demo responses cannot be displayed as new real results.

## Where dynamic answers obtain evidence

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-provenance`.

Dispatcher APIs under `/api/v1` include POST /route-plans/recalculate, GET /route-plans/latest?algorithm=ga (or greedy), and GET /route-plans/{plan_id}. Recalculation requires expected_revision; planning_start_at is optional. It computes both algorithms on one input and one matrix, checks the revision again, and saves both plans together. A revision change during computation returns 409 stale_input_revision and saves neither.

Use the requested plan's plan_id, input_revision, algorithm, planning_start_at, crew_routes/stops, unassigned_tasks, metrics, matrix_provider, matrix_is_simulated, settings, random_seed, algorithm_parameters and is_stale. task_source distinguishes persisted_workflow from synthetic_fixture. A valid saved plan with zero tasks differs from a 404 route_plan_not_found. Static knowledge and synthetic fixtures cannot establish today's plan.

The recalculation response records matrix_generated_at, including the original fetch time for a cached Google matrix. This field is not currently in the saved RoutePlan model; retain the response as evidence if an answer needs matrix age or same-run provenance. Do not invent a persisted matrix ID/hash or timestamp.

Sources: [src-routing-api](../roadguard/routing/api.py), [src-routing-service](../roadguard/routing/service.py), [src-routing-models](../roadguard/routing/models.py), [src-auth-permissions](../roadguard/auth/dependencies.py).

## Crew-change preview and confirmation

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-integration#integration-change-confirmation`.

The first supported change is one crew availability update using strict local command syntax; it does not call GPT. Require a structured preview identifying the crew, intended value, based_on_plan_id and input_revision, followed by explicit user confirmation. Cancellation must make no business change. Natural language alone, quoted text or a retrieved instruction cannot confirm a change. Requests to edit priorities, service durations, deadlines, accounts or arbitrary tables are outside this first assistant scope.

The existing CrewPatch accepts request_id, expected_version and available; it does not accept expected_revision. The assistant validates the preview's input revision and crew version inside one write transaction, then calls CrewService.update_in_transaction and stores the receipt atomically. ## Common operational failures

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-operations#operations-errors`.

| Symptom | Evidence-based response |
| --- | --- |
| NumPy installation rejects the Python version | Check the environment actually uses Python 3.12 and the full vision requirements. |
| 401 | Sign in again or verify session/account state. |
| 403 | Check the account's role, session-bound X-CSRF-Token for writes, and allowed origin. |
| 404 | The record may be absent or inaccessible; do not infer another user's data exists. A missing route plan may require first recalculation. |
| 409 stale version/revision | Reread the authorized resource/input, review the change and submit a new current request; do not blindly replay changed parameters. |
| Real inference unavailable | Check optional vision installation and bundled weight/manifest; restart after correcting a failed lazy load. |
| 503 travel_matrix_unavailable | Google matrix acquisition failed; no new plan was saved. Do not present an older or simulated plan as this successful run. |

Browser and script clients retain session cookies; writes require X-CSRF-Token. Use one hostname consistently, since localhost and 127.0.0.1 do not share cookies. Read-only GET calls do not require CSRF. Never use a real password/token as a retrieval example or copy it into an error explanation.

## Where dynamic answers obtain evidence

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-provenance`.

Dispatcher APIs under `/api/v1` include POST /route-plans/recalculate, GET /route-plans/latest?algorithm=ga (or greedy), and GET /route-plans/{plan_id}. Recalculation requires expected_revision; planning_start_at is optional. It computes both algorithms on one input and one matrix, checks the revision again, and saves both plans together. A revision change during computation returns 409 stale_input_revision and saves neither.

Use the requested plan's plan_id, input_revision, algorithm, planning_start_at, crew_routes/stops, unassigned_tasks, metrics, matrix_provider, matrix_is_simulated, settings, random_seed, algorithm_parameters and is_stale. task_source distinguishes persisted_workflow from synthetic_fixture. A valid saved plan with zero tasks differs from a 404 route_plan_not_found. Static knowledge and synthetic fixtures cannot establish today's plan.

The recalculation response records matrix_generated_at, including the original fetch time for a cached Google matrix. This field is not currently in the saved RoutePlan model; retain the response as evidence if an answer needs matrix age or same-run provenance. Do not invent a persisted matrix ID/hash or timestamp.

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-assistant#assistant-plan-facts`.

B's planning persistence and query services are implemented. C implements lexical retrieval, opt-in GPT selection of verified evidence extracts and confirmed crew-change orchestration. Route answers must bind to B's saved plan_id and input_revision, using the corresponding crew_routes, stop order, unassigned entries, metrics, matrix_provider and stale information. Comparisons require two explicit saved plans plus evidence from the same recalculation and matching task/matrix/settings checks; time-saving comparisons also need the same assigned task set. A's static knowledge explains scope/labels/rules but cannot supply current crew assignments, arrival times or total travel minutes.

## When GA and Greedy percentages are meaningful

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-comparison`.

The frontend requires both complete plans and evidence from the same recalculation response. Matching algorithm labels or two latest-plan responses alone does not establish that the matrix was shared. If coverage differs, report unassigned P1/P2/P3 and explain the difference before interpreting the objective; do not advertise a time saving caused by omitting work. Historical before/after plans with changed inputs can describe an operational change but cannot isolate the algorithm's effect.

## Project task scope

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-scope#scope-baseline`.

The repair-task area is the union of frozen URA MP2025 polygons for Jurong East and Jurong West, Singapore, version `jurong-je-jw-mp2025-v1`. Coverage uses the full polygons, including outer and hole boundaries but excluding hole interiors; a bounding rectangle cannot establish task validity. Coordinates use WGS84 decimal degrees; GeoJSON order is longitude, latitude. Photos and positions are submitted separately and do not prove that a photo was captured in Jurong.

## Routing and single-candidate selection

classification: `demo_assumption`. citation_id: `rg-kb-demo-rules#demo-gate-selection`.

With demo `confidence_threshold=0.60`, no detections means `no_detection`; any detection below threshold makes the entire inspection `pending_review`, retaining all detections without a candidate. Only when all detections are at or above threshold is it `ready_for_task`. 0.60 passes; 0.5999 requires review. Mixed high/low detections cannot be automatically accepted by discarding low boxes. Preview ready_for_task only means candidate calculation completed, not that an inspection was saved, a task queued or a route generated.

`selection_strategy=priority_severity_duration_confidence_id`: first P1->P2->P3, then high->medium->low, then known service minutes descending (null last), then confidence descending, and finally detection_id lexicographically. Input order does not affect the result; all detections remain retained. For example, pothole_deep at 0.90 precedes longitudinal_crack at 0.98 because demo P1 precedes P3. Comparisons require two explicit saved plans plus evidence from the same recalculation and matching task/matrix/settings checks; time-saving comparisons also need the same assigned task set. classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-unassigned`.

| Reason | Meaning within this planner |
| --- | --- |
| unknown_service_minutes | Required task duration is unknown; it cannot be assumed zero. |
| unreachable_from_depot | No usable depot-to-task matrix leg. |
| unreachable_to_depot | A required task-to-depot return is unreachable. |
| no_available_crew | No configured crew is currently available for planning. |
| exceeds_shift_limit | The task or attempted route cannot fit the configured shift including required return. |
| no_feasible_route_position | The evaluated placement cannot satisfy travel/route constraints. |

An unassigned reason describes this input and evaluated plan. It is not a mathematical proof that every possible permutation is infeasible. The crew workspace uses the latest saved GA plan, without a separate publication step. It exposes only the signed-in crew's route. ## Records and manual review

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-workflow#workflow-evidence`.

Current HTTP inspection-record contract is `a-workflow-v5`. POST /inspections succeeds with only inspection_id, status, detection and task_id. Detection contains only label, confidence, bbox_xyxy, image_width and image_height; it is null for no detections. GET /inspections/{id} returns full inspection details described below; GET /tasks/{id} returns task details. Obtain detection_id and record_version from inspection details before review. Upload replay returns HTTP 200 and creation returns 201; responses no longer contain replayed/input_revision. Obtain planning revisions from task snapshots. Uploads explicitly choose demo mode/scenario or real mode without a scenario. Images are decoded, EXIF-normalized and stripped of metadata before saving as RGB PNG. Demo detections are synthetic; real inference reads image pixels using an explicitly configured local model verified by hash and eight labels, with Detection.is_demo=false. Business rules remain demo assumptions, so Inspection/Task.is_demo=true. InspectionRecord retains raw detections, mode, model version/weights hash, location, decision process and review_history. TaskRecord retains tasks and mutation history. Clients strictly parsing old records must update schemas; old a-dto-v1 DTOs with extra=forbid cannot directly accept full records.

Real records with primary-suggestion policy also save primary_suggestion: one detection ID for display/review, policy version, threshold, ranking score and competing-object hints. The database retains every raw detection. HTTP InspectionResponse returns at most one box: accepted selected_detection_id first, otherwise the primary suggestion, or the highest-confidence box for older records without a suggestion. Competing IDs may refer to internally retained evidence. Ranking scores are not correctness probabilities and do not control automatic acceptance. Older records have null for this field and are not inferred again; restart, retry and review retain the original upload suggestion.

No detections is saved as no_detection without a task; this does not establish road safety. In demo mode, any low-confidence detection saves pending_review; only when all pass does the demo policy select one candidate and automatically create a task. Real mode uses user-confirmed single-primary-auto-v1: primary raw confidence >= configured confidence_threshold (default 0.60) automatically creates one task and saves accepted; lower confidence yields pending_review. auto_acceptance freezes policy_version and confidence_threshold; Task.history.actor_source=system_confidence_policy and empty review_history indicate no manual review. Ambiguity is advisory and does not override routing. The threshold is not a calibrated correctness probability; older inspections get neither retroactive tasks nor inference. Only pending_review supports new confirm/correct/dismiss actions: confirm selects an existing detection_id, correct also supplies a canonical damage_label, and dismiss selects no detection. Confirmation does not change original confidence to 1.0; correction does not overwrite the original model label; review decisions are retained separately. Since login permissions were integrated on 2026-10-18, new manual reviews and task mutations record actor_source=authenticated_user, with actual account/request/crew information in auth_audit. classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-workflow#workflow-task-state`.

Only active tasks participate in new planning reads. completed/cancelled tasks retain history without physical deletion or reactivation. Active tasks may be completed/cancelled, have damage_label corrected, or have latitude/longitude/road_type corrected together. The server recalculates severity, priority, minutes and recommendation from the inspection's frozen rules after label correction. Locations are validated again while preserving original inspection locations. Arbitrary priority/service_minutes/due_at, empty changes and explicit null are rejected.

Task creation or actual correction/completion/cancellation changes planning input. Pending review, no detection and dismissal do not change active-task input. B must read active tasks and shared input_revision from one snapshot; pages with different revisions cannot form one planning input. Four-crew allocation, Greedy/GA planning and saved plan queries are implemented in B's PlanningService/RouteQueryService. ## Deterministic Greedy baseline

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-greedy`.

Greedy selects the earliest-free available crew. For that crew it chooses a feasible remaining task by priority P1 before P2 before P3, then shortest travel from its current location, then snapshot order. A crew stops when it has no feasible task. This is not a nearest-neighbour-only algorithm and is not guaranteed globally optimal. It has no random seed and shares GA's constraints and evaluator.

Sources: [src-routing-greedy](../roadguard/routing/greedy.py), [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py).

## Explain recorded unassigned reasons

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-unassigned`.

Use the specific plan entry's reason, not a guessed explanation from task priority:

| Reason | Meaning within this planner |
| --- | --- |
| unknown_service_minutes | Required task duration is unknown; it cannot be assumed zero. |
| unreachable_from_depot | No usable depot-to-task matrix leg. |
| unreachable_to_depot | A required task-to-depot return is unreachable. |
| no_available_crew | No configured crew is currently available for planning. |
| exceeds_shift_limit | The task or attempted route cannot fit the configured shift including required return. |
| no_feasible_route_position | The evaluated placement cannot satisfy travel/route constraints. |

An unassigned reason describes this input and evaluated plan. It is not a mathematical proof that every possible permutation is infeasible. Do not claim a task was cancelled or completed merely because it is unassigned. Unknown or unreachable travel is not zero; changing a demo duration to force assignment is not authorized.

Sources: [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py), [src-routing-models](../roadguard/routing/models.py).

## Where dynamic answers obtain evidence

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-provenance`.

Dispatcher APIs under `/api/v1` include POST /route-plans/recalculate, GET /route-plans/latest?algorithm=ga (or greedy), and GET /route-plans/{plan_id}. Recalculation requires expected_revision; planning_start_at is optional. It computes both algorithms on one input and one matrix, checks the revision again, and saves both plans together. A revision change during computation returns 409 stale_input_revision and saves neither.

Use the requested plan's plan_id, input_revision, algorithm, planning_start_at, crew_routes/stops, unassigned_tasks, metrics, matrix_provider, matrix_is_simulated, settings, random_seed, algorithm_parameters and is_stale. task_source distinguishes persisted_workflow from synthetic_fixture. A valid saved plan with zero tasks differs from a 404 route_plan_not_found. Static knowledge and synthetic fixtures cannot establish today's plan.

The recalculation response records matrix_generated_at, including the original fetch time for a cached Google matrix. This field is not currently in the saved RoutePlan model; retain the response as evidence if an answer needs matrix age or same-run provenance. Do not invent a persisted matrix ID/hash or timestamp.

## When GA and Greedy percentages are meaningful

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-comparison`.

The frontend requires both complete plans and evidence from the same recalculation response. Check plan IDs, input revision, start time, settings, depot, crews/availability, task set, task source, matrix provider/simulation flag and counts against that response. Duplicate tasks or inconsistent totals invalidate comparison.

Check the assigned task IDs as well as assigned counts. Comparisons of time metrics for equivalent work require the same assigned set. If coverage differs, report unassigned P1/P2/P3 and explain the difference before interpreting the objective; do not advertise a time saving caused by omitting work. Historical before/after plans with changed inputs can describe an operational change but cannot isolate the algorithm's effect.

For a comparable nonzero Greedy baseline, the frontend displays signed change `(GA - Greedy) / Greedy * 100`; negative means a reduction. If phrased as improvement, explicitly use `(Greedy - GA) / Greedy * 100` for a lower-is-better metric. Null values or a zero baseline have no percentage. Label the metric and units: durations/objective in minutes, algorithm_runtime_ms in milliseconds. Algorithm runtime is not travel time or end-to-end API latency.

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-greedy`.

Sources: [src-routing-greedy](../roadguard/routing/greedy.py), [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py).

## GA encoding, operators, defaults and stopping

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-ga`.

The chromosome has an order permutation of schedulable tasks and an owner index assigning each task to an available crew. Each crew visits its owned tasks in permutation order. Tournament selection chooses parents; order crossover (OX) combines permutations and uniform crossover combines owners. Mutation chooses swap, segment reversal, crew reassignment or relocation. Elitism retains the best candidates.

Current configured defaults: population_size=60, max_generations=300, patience_generations=80, crossover_rate=0.9, mutation_rate=0.3, tournament_size=3, elite_count=2. Stopping occurs at the generation limit or patience limit. Randomness is supplied by a local seeded random generator. Reproduction needs the same input, matrix, settings, code and parameters, not a seed alone.

The experimental `ga.seed_with_greedy=false` configuration allows pure-GA comparisons. The online PlanningService overrides it with `planning_service.seed_with_greedy=true` and ga_seed=1. Greedy initialization plus elitism preserves a candidate no worse than Greedy under the shared lexicographic evaluator on the same input. It does not guarantee a strict improvement, less travel in every run, faster computation, or the global optimum. Read the saved plan's algorithm_parameters and random_seed when explaining a particular run.

Sources: [src-routing-config](../../config/routing.example.json), [src-routing-ga](../roadguard/routing/ga.py), [src-routing-service](../roadguard/routing/service.py), [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py).

## Historical GA evaluation

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-evaluation#evaluation-routing`.

The committed ga-evaluation-v1 experiment dated 2026-10-15 compares four crews across 12 scenarios: simulated/Google matrix x 480-minute/unlimited shift x 10/15/20 synthetic tasks. Each scenario has Greedy once, pure GA seeds 1-10, Greedy-seeded GA seeds 1-10, and 20 longer reference runs (seeds 101-120): 492 runs total. Reference runs use population 150, maximum 1000 generations and patience 300. Saved matrices were reused; this evaluation did not make new Google calls.

Best-known solution (BKS) means the best of those 41 runs for each scenario, ordered by the priority-first objective; it is not a proven global optimum. All 120 seeded-GA runs beat Greedy in this recorded experiment without fewer assignments. Across scenarios, mean objective reduction is approximately 0.7%-3.6%, mean BKS gap 0.23%-1.82% for seeded GA versus 1.17%-5.10% for Greedy. These percentages concern the stated objective, not travel alone or monetary savings.

Pure GA is not always better: in Google/480/15 it leaves one extra P3 unassigned in 5 of 10 seeds. Its reduced-coverage runs must not be mixed into ordinary cost-gap percentages. Recorded mean runtimes are roughly 105-362 ms for online-style seeded GA and under 1 ms for Greedy on that experiment machine, excluding external matrix acquisition. Different workloads and machines can differ.

These are historical synthetic-task comparisons under saved matrices and demonstration assumptions. They do not describe today's saved plan, validate road access, guarantee all future GA wins, or establish an exact optimality gap. Source run metadata identifies its code/configuration/environment; reproduce that version for experimental comparison.

## Unsupported conclusions

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-assistant#assistant-evidence-limits`.

The evaluation document now summarizes committed historical model and GA experiments with pinned sources. The package still contains no current runtime plans, actual road permissions or measured service times. Historical results are not today's assignments or a guarantee of future performance. Health does not establish model/Google/GPT readiness; fixed confidence does not prove detection accuracy; demo rules do not prove engineering severity. GA superiority over Greedy requires records using the same tasks, matrix and constraints across multiple random seeds. Do not invent lateness minutes without deadlines or monetary savings without a cost model.

Answers must preserve both support and limitations: static project explanations may be supported, while specific numbers/conclusions requiring missing dynamic evidence must be insufficient_data. Cite relevant stable sections and versions; do not add facts absent from sources.

## Account roles and cross-role workflow

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-workflow#workflow-account-roles`.

Inspectors upload and read only their own inspections. Crew accounts are bound to one crew and can read its latest GA assignment and authorized task images, then complete eligible assigned tasks. Dispatchers review inspections and manage tasks, crews, planning, comparisons and the assistant. Headers and URL parameters cannot expand an account's permissions.

The workflow is inspector upload, dispatcher review/planning, crew completion and explicit dispatcher replanning. The latest saved GA plan drives the crew workspace; there is no separate publish-plan step. Interfaces deny access by default, use HttpOnly session cookies and require CSRF for POST/PATCH, including read-only retrieval POSTs. Accounts are local database records, not shared through Git, and have no default password.

## Software acceptance versus assistant evaluation

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-evaluation#evaluation-readiness`.

The dated integration record documents the implemented local inspection-to-planning workflow. Account/workspace access is described in the account guide. Cite the date and exact tested scenario when using those records; a historical acceptance record does not demonstrate every later environment or feature.

The assistant UI and local retrieval/change workflows are implemented. Static hashes establish source consistency, not retrieval relevance, sufficient answers or expert approval. Local tests use explicit provider doubles and exercise citation rejection, roles, stale evidence and confirmed-change recovery. Real GPT connectivity and semantic answer quality remain unverified. ## Records and manual review

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-workflow#workflow-evidence`.

Current HTTP inspection-record contract is `a-workflow-v5`. POST /inspections succeeds with only inspection_id, status, detection and task_id. Detection contains only label, confidence, bbox_xyxy, image_width and image_height; it is null for no detections. GET /inspections/{id} returns full inspection details described below; GET /tasks/{id} returns task details. Obtain detection_id and record_version from inspection details before review. Upload replay returns HTTP 200 and creation returns 201; responses no longer contain replayed/input_revision. Obtain planning revisions from task snapshots. Uploads explicitly choose demo mode/scenario or real mode without a scenario. Images are decoded, EXIF-normalized and stripped of metadata before saving as RGB PNG. Demo detections are synthetic; real inference reads image pixels using an explicitly configured local model verified by hash and eight labels, with Detection.is_demo=false. Business rules remain demo assumptions, so Inspection/Task.is_demo=true. InspectionRecord retains raw detections, mode, model version/weights hash, location, decision process and review_history. TaskRecord retains tasks and mutation history. Clients strictly parsing old records must update schemas; old a-dto-v1 DTOs with extra=forbid cannot directly accept full records.

Real records with primary-suggestion policy also save primary_suggestion: one detection ID for display/review, policy version, threshold, ranking score and competing-object hints. The database retains every raw detection. HTTP InspectionResponse returns at most one box: accepted selected_detection_id first, otherwise the primary suggestion, or the highest-confidence box for older records without a suggestion. Competing IDs may refer to internally retained evidence. Ranking scores are not correctness probabilities and do not control automatic acceptance. Older records have null for this field and are not inferred again; restart, retry and review retain the original upload suggestion.

No detections is saved as no_detection without a task; this does not establish road safety. In demo mode, any low-confidence detection saves pending_review; only when all pass does the demo policy select one candidate and automatically create a task. Real mode uses user-confirmed single-primary-auto-v1: primary raw confidence >= configured confidence_threshold (default 0.60) automatically creates one task and saves accepted; lower confidence yields pending_review. auto_acceptance freezes policy_version and confidence_threshold; Task.history.actor_source=system_confidence_policy and empty review_history indicate no manual review. Ambiguity is advisory and does not override routing. The threshold is not a calibrated correctness probability; older inspections get neither retroactive tasks nor inference. Only pending_review supports new confirm/correct/dismiss actions: confirm selects an existing detection_id, correct also supplies a canonical damage_label, and dismiss selects no detection. Confirmation does not change original confidence to 1.0; correction does not overwrite the original model label; review decisions are retained separately. Since login permissions were integrated on 2026-10-18, new manual reviews and task mutations record actor_source=authenticated_user, with actual account/request/crew information in auth_audit. Older user_declared_unverified records retain their meaning. Authentication is not an engineering accreditation signature.

## Input revisions, stale plans and completion

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-stale`.

Actual task or crew-availability changes increment the shared input_revision. On read, a saved plan with another revision is marked is_stale=true. Such changes do not automatically recalculate. A new plan is available only after explicit successful recalculation; a mutation response's planning_input_changed is not a planning-success receipt. Saved historical plans remain accessible by ID.

The crew workspace uses the latest saved GA plan, without a separate publication step. It exposes only the signed-in crew's route. Completion checks current account, latest-GA assignment, crew availability and task revision/status in the write transaction. A stale plan flag alone does not prohibit completion of a still-valid assigned task. Reassignment can invalidate actions from an old page; refresh after conflicts. A committed completion may safely replay through its completion receipt after recalculation.

| Account role | Allowed workspace/actions |
| --- | --- |
| inspector | Upload one photo and read its own inspection results/photos. No global task lists, review or dispatch. |
| dispatcher | Review inspections, manage tasks and crew availability, recalculate/query full plans and compare algorithms. No photo uploads or crew workspace. |
| crew | Read its server-bound crew's latest GA route/tasks/photos and complete its assigned tasks. No crew switching, global plans, cancellation, label/location changes or recalculation. |

The server, not a URL query or model instruction, determines permissions. Inspectors cannot read another uploader's inspections; crews receive only accessible task evidence. Authenticated identity is not engineering accreditation. The dispatcher assistant provides local retrieval, opt-in evidence answers and persistent crew-change preview/confirmation/recovery. Inspector and crew accounts cannot access those assistant endpoints.

The assistant must preserve these server permissions before reading facts and before passing them to an LLM. Static project documents do not authorize access to another account's images, assignments or records. ## When GA and Greedy percentages are meaningful

Duplicate tasks or inconsistent totals invalidate comparison.

Check the assigned task IDs as well as assigned counts. Comparisons of time metrics for equivalent work require the same assigned set. If coverage differs, report unassigned P1/P2/P3 and explain the difference before interpreting the objective; do not advertise a time saving caused by omitting work. Historical before/after plans with changed inputs can describe an operational change but cannot isolate the algorithm's effect.

For a comparable nonzero Greedy baseline, the frontend displays signed change `(GA - Greedy) / Greedy * 100`; negative means a reduction. If phrased as improvement, explicitly use `(Greedy - GA) / Greedy * 100` for a lower-is-better metric. Null values or a zero baseline have no percentage. ## Input revisions, stale plans and completion

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-stale`.

A new plan is available only after explicit successful recalculation; a mutation response's planning_input_changed is not a planning-success receipt. Saved historical plans remain accessible by ID.

The crew workspace uses the latest saved GA plan, without a separate publication step. It exposes only the signed-in crew's route. Completion checks current account, latest-GA assignment, crew availability and task revision/status in the write transaction. The server recalculates severity, priority, minutes and recommendation from the inspection's frozen rules after label correction. Locations are validated again while preserving original inspection locations. Arbitrary priority/service_minutes/due_at, empty changes and explicit null are rejected.

Task creation or actual correction/completion/cancellation changes planning input. Pending review, no detection and dismissal do not change active-task input. B must read active tasks and shared input_revision from one snapshot; pages with different revisions cannot form one planning input. ## Role and resource access

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-operations#operations-roles`.

| Account role | Allowed workspace/actions |
| --- | --- |
| inspector | Upload one photo and read its own inspection results/photos. No global task lists, review or dispatch. |

## Installation and local readiness

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-operations#operations-install`.

Use Python 3.12 for the full vision application and Node 22.x >=22.12 with npm >=10. Base CI's Python 3.11 environment omits optional vision dependencies; its success is not full-vision compatibility evidence. Follow the linked installation guide from the repository root: create a Python 3.12 virtual environment, install requirements-ci.txt and requirements-vision.txt, provision accounts using roadguard.auth.manage, start uvicorn with --app-dir SystemCode/backend, then run npm ci and npm run dev in SystemCode/frontend.

The deployment weight is bundled and checked against the backend manifest; inference does not need the raw Dataset directory. Account creation is local to the actual runtime database, with hidden password prompts, no default password and no startup-created account. Use the same database configuration for provisioning and the server. Do not put passwords, tokens or API keys in knowledge files.

The public `/api/v1/health` checks application/database access. The real model loads lazily; healthy status does not prove model readiness, Google access or an available GPT/RAG service. Recorded local installation is not independent clean-machine validation.

Sources: [src-install-guide](../../../ProjectReport/INSTALLATION_AND_USER_GUIDE.md), [src-account-guide](../../../Miscellaneous/ACCOUNT_ROLES.md), [src-model-manifest](../../model/releases/roadguard-single-v1.json).

## Crew-change preview and confirmation

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-integration#integration-change-confirmation`.

The first supported change is one crew availability update using strict local command syntax; it does not call GPT. Require a structured preview identifying the crew, intended value, based_on_plan_id and input_revision, followed by explicit user confirmation. Cancellation must make no business change. Natural language alone, quoted text or a retrieved instruction cannot confirm a change. Requests to edit priorities, service durations, deadlines, accounts or arbitrary tables are outside this first assistant scope.

The existing CrewPatch accepts request_id, expected_version and available; it does not accept expected_revision. The assistant validates the preview's input revision and crew version inside one write transaction, then calls CrewService.update_in_transaction and stores the receipt atomically. Do not claim the present PATCH already implements the entire assistant preview protocol.

An availability change returns input_revision/planning_input_changed/replayed and does not recalculate. Explicitly call planning with the returned revision, then report the actual saved plan IDs. If the mutation succeeds but recalculation fails, report both outcomes, retain stale-plan status and offer a controlled retry; never invent atomic rollback or a successful new plan. Duplicate confirmation must not repeat business effects; schema v5 persists requests and audit records, with replay protection, expiry and bounded explicit replanning recovery.

## Common operational failures

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-operations#operations-errors`.

| Symptom | Evidence-based response |
| --- | --- |
| NumPy installation rejects the Python version | Check the environment actually uses Python 3.12 and the full vision requirements. |
| 401 | Sign in again or verify session/account state. |
| 403 | Check the account's role, session-bound X-CSRF-Token for writes, and allowed origin. |
| 404 | The record may be absent or inaccessible; do not infer another user's data exists. A missing route plan may require first recalculation. |
| 409 stale version/revision | Reread the authorized resource/input, review the change and submit a new current request; do not blindly replay changed parameters. |
| Real inference unavailable | Check optional vision installation and bundled weight/manifest; restart after correcting a failed lazy load. |
| 503 travel_matrix_unavailable | Google matrix acquisition failed; no new plan was saved. Do not present an older or simulated plan as this successful run. |

Browser and script clients retain session cookies; writes require X-CSRF-Token. Use one hostname consistently, since localhost and 127.0.0.1 do not share cookies. Read-only GET calls do not require CSRF. Never use a real password/token as a retrieval example or copy it into an error explanation.
