## GA encoding, operators, defaults and stopping

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-ga`.

The chromosome has an order permutation of schedulable tasks and an owner index assigning each task to an available crew. Each crew visits its owned tasks in permutation order. Tournament selection chooses parents; order crossover (OX) combines permutations and uniform crossover combines owners. Mutation chooses swap, segment reversal, crew reassignment or relocation. Elitism retains the best candidates.

Current configured defaults: population_size=60, max_generations=300, patience_generations=80, crossover_rate=0.9, mutation_rate=0.3, tournament_size=3, elite_count=2. Stopping occurs at the generation limit or patience limit. Randomness is supplied by a local seeded random generator. Reproduction needs the same input, matrix, settings, code and parameters, not a seed alone.

The experimental `ga.seed_with_greedy=false` configuration allows pure-GA comparisons. The online PlanningService overrides it with `planning_service.seed_with_greedy=true` and ga_seed=1. Greedy initialization plus elitism preserves a candidate no worse than Greedy under the shared lexicographic evaluator on the same input. It does not guarantee a strict improvement, less travel in every run, faster computation, or the global optimum. Read the saved plan's algorithm_parameters and random_seed when explaining a particular run.

Sources: [src-routing-config](../../config/routing.example.json), [src-routing-ga](../roadguard/routing/ga.py), [src-routing-service](../roadguard/routing/service.py), [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py).

## Deterministic Greedy baseline

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-greedy`.

Greedy selects the earliest-free available crew. For that crew it chooses a feasible remaining task by priority P1 before P2 before P3, then shortest travel from its current location, then snapshot order. A crew stops when it has no feasible task. This is not a nearest-neighbour-only algorithm and is not guaranteed globally optimal. It has no random seed and shares GA's constraints and evaluator.

Sources: [src-routing-greedy](../roadguard/routing/greedy.py), [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py).

## Suggested ingestion and source lifecycle

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-integration#integration-ingestion`.

The local loader validates the knowledge package on every request. A separate setup command embeds token-bounded passages and builds a versioned persistent Chroma collection; requests never download weights or rebuild indexes. Read manifest.json and verify all pinned document/source/guide/acceptance digests before indexing. Index only manifest-listed knowledge sections, using explicit anchors as passage boundaries. Retain title, document_id, section_id, citation_id, document_version, package_version, classification, source_ids and raw-file hash. If a section must be subdivided, retain its parent citation and mark the child position; do not separate a claim from its demo/status limitations.

Treat unchanged labels and business rules as versioned evidence. Changed files invalidate prior digests and require a new reviewed package; never relabel old chunks as current. Build a replacement index before switching active versions and retain enough metadata to audit historical answers. Runtime records retain their frozen rule versions; if matching evidence is absent, request it instead of substituting today's table.

Mutable context_sources explain background and responsibility but do not override hashed executable/configuration facts. Do not bulk-index the whole repository, historical reports, secrets, uploaded images, SQLite files or synthetic runtime fixtures as current operational truth. English source IDs and schema terms remain unchanged when an answer is translated into Chinese. The current baseline uses local multilingual E5 vectors and cosine ranking with explicit limits. Retrieval sends selected passages to the evidence selector; cross-language coverage and answer sufficiency still require evaluation.

Sources: [context-team](../../../Miscellaneous/TEAM_WORK_ALLOCATION.md), [context-agents](../../../AGENTS.md), [src-workflow-schema](../roadguard/schemas/workflow.py), [src-workflow-service](../roadguard/inspections/service.py).

Implementation sources: [src-vector-store](../roadguard/assistant/vector_store.py), [src-embedding](../roadguard/assistant/embedding.py), [src-semantic-retrieval](../roadguard/assistant/retrieval.py), [src-retrieval-setup](../roadguard/assistant/VECTOR_RETRIEVAL.md).

## Implemented planning and shared constraints

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-input`.

Both Greedy and the custom genetic algorithm (GA) are implemented. PlanningService reads all active tasks and all four configured crews in one database snapshot. Saved task priority and service_minutes are inputs; the planner does not infer them again from photos or substitute today's rule table. Only available crews receive tasks. Both algorithms use the same travel matrix, depot, settings and RoutingProblem evaluator.

Each input task must appear exactly once, either in a crew's ordered stops or in unassigned_tasks. Unknown service duration, inaccessible travel and shift limits are constraints, not permission to drop tasks silently. All available crews begin at the same depot at planning_start_at. This is static replanning from a common start; there is no live vehicle tracking, in-transit dispatch or task time-window model.

Sources: [src-routing-service](../roadguard/routing/service.py), [src-routing-models](../roadguard/routing/models.py), [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py).

## Where dynamic answers obtain evidence

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-provenance`.

Dispatcher APIs under `/api/v1` include POST /route-plans/recalculate, GET /route-plans/latest?algorithm=ga (or greedy), and GET /route-plans/{plan_id}. Recalculation requires expected_revision; planning_start_at is optional. It computes both algorithms on one input and one matrix, checks the revision again, and saves both plans together. A revision change during computation returns 409 stale_input_revision and saves neither.

Use the requested plan's plan_id, input_revision, algorithm, planning_start_at, crew_routes/stops, unassigned_tasks, metrics, matrix_provider, matrix_is_simulated, settings, random_seed, algorithm_parameters and is_stale. task_source distinguishes persisted_workflow from synthetic_fixture. A valid saved plan with zero tasks differs from a 404 route_plan_not_found. Static knowledge and synthetic fixtures cannot establish today's plan.

The recalculation response records matrix_generated_at, including the original fetch time for a cached Google matrix. This field is not currently in the saved RoutePlan model; retain the response as evidence if an answer needs matrix age or same-run provenance. Do not invent a persisted matrix ID/hash or timestamp.

## Historical GA evaluation

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-evaluation#evaluation-routing`.

The committed ga-evaluation-v1 experiment dated 2026-10-15 compares four crews across 12 scenarios: simulated/Google matrix x 480-minute/unlimited shift x 10/15/20 synthetic tasks. Each scenario has Greedy once, pure GA seeds 1-10, Greedy-seeded GA seeds 1-10, and 20 longer reference runs (seeds 101-120): 492 runs total. Reference runs use population 150, maximum 1000 generations and patience 300. Saved matrices were reused; this evaluation did not make new Google calls.

Best-known solution (BKS) means the best of those 41 runs for each scenario, ordered by the priority-first objective; it is not a proven global optimum. All 120 seeded-GA runs beat Greedy in this recorded experiment without fewer assignments. Across scenarios, mean objective reduction is approximately 0.7%-3.6%, mean BKS gap 0.23%-1.82% for seeded GA versus 1.17%-5.10% for Greedy. These percentages concern the stated objective, not travel alone or monetary savings.

Pure GA is not always better: in Google/480/15 it leaves one extra P3 unassigned in 5 of 10 seeds. Its reduced-coverage runs must not be mixed into ordinary cost-gap percentages. Recorded mean runtimes are roughly 105-362 ms for online-style seeded GA and under 1 ms for Greedy on that experiment machine, excluding external matrix acquisition. Different workloads and machines can differ.

These are historical synthetic-task comparisons under saved matrices and demonstration assumptions. They do not describe today's saved plan, validate road access, guarantee all future GA wins, or establish an exact optimality gap. Source run metadata identifies its code/configuration/environment; reproduce that version for experimental comparison.

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-ga`.

The chromosome has an order permutation of schedulable tasks and an owner index assigning each task to an available crew. Each crew visits its owned tasks in permutation order. Tournament selection chooses parents; order crossover (OX) combines permutations and uniform crossover combines owners. Mutation chooses swap, segment reversal, crew reassignment or relocation. Elitism retains the best candidates.

Current configured defaults: population_size=60, max_generations=300, patience_generations=80, crossover_rate=0.9, mutation_rate=0.3, tournament_size=3, elite_count=2. Stopping occurs at the generation limit or patience limit. Randomness is supplied by a local seeded random generator. Reproduction needs the same input, matrix, settings, code and parameters, not a seed alone.

The experimental `ga.seed_with_greedy=false` configuration allows pure-GA comparisons. The online PlanningService overrides it with `planning_service.seed_with_greedy=true` and ga_seed=1. Greedy initialization plus elitism preserves a candidate no worse than Greedy under the shared lexicographic evaluator on the same input. It does not guarantee a strict improvement, less travel in every run, faster computation, or the global optimum. Read the saved plan's algorithm_parameters and random_seed when explaining a particular run.

Sources: [src-routing-config](../../config/routing.example.json), [src-routing-ga](../roadguard/routing/ga.py), [src-routing-service](../roadguard/routing/service.py), [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py).

## Routing and single-candidate selection

classification: `demo_assumption`. citation_id: `rg-kb-demo-rules#demo-gate-selection`.

The following applies to stateless demo previews and explicit demo uploads. Real uploads use the model-selected primary box's raw confidence and do not apply demo multi-candidate ordering. With demo `confidence_threshold=0.60`, no detections means `no_detection`; any detection below threshold makes the entire inspection `pending_review`, retaining all detections without a candidate. Only when all detections are at or above threshold is it `ready_for_task`. 0.60 passes; 0.5999 requires review. Mixed high/low detections cannot be automatically accepted by discarding low boxes. Preview ready_for_task only means candidate calculation completed, not that an inspection was saved, a task queued or a route generated.

`selection_strategy=priority_severity_duration_confidence_id`: first P1->P2->P3, then high->medium->low, then known service minutes descending (null last), then confidence descending, and finally detection_id lexicographically. Input order does not affect the result; all detections remain retained. For example, pothole_deep at 0.90 precedes longitudinal_crack at 0.98 because demo P1 precedes P3. At most one task per inspection is also a demo policy, not a formal multiple-damage dispatch rule.

Sources: [src-demo-rules](../../config/demo_rules.example.json), [src-rule-service](../roadguard/rules/service.py), [src-workflow-service](../roadguard/inspections/service.py).

## Unknown values and provenance

classification: `demo_assumption`. citation_id: `rg-kb-demo-rules#demo-null-provenance`.

Unknown service_minutes is null, never zero; all eight current configured durations are demo minutes. Task due_at remains null, so no deadlines or lateness metrics are generated. Inspections freeze the complete rule snapshot; reviews and task-label corrections use it rather than new configuration after restart. Preserve Detection model_version/is_demo when citing detections, read Inspection decision_trace for decisions and retain Task rule_version/is_demo when citing tasks. Do not assume Task itself contains a model version or full decision process. Explicit demo uploads use named synthetic scenarios; only real uploads invoke the actual detector. Service minutes are neither a deadline nor travel time and are not divided by four because there are four crews.

This package's static table explains demo-rules-v2 only; runtime records may use overridden configurations with other versions. Do not use this package or the latest rule table to recalculate or explain older tasks from another version. Use each record's saved rule version, decision_trace and history; acknowledge insufficient_data without matching evidence.

Sources: [src-demo-rules](../../config/demo_rules.example.json), [src-workflow-service](../roadguard/inspections/service.py), [src-workflow-schema](../roadguard/schemas/workflow.py).

## Primary-label metrics and confidence are different

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-evaluation#evaluation-vision`.

The deployed experimental model is yolo11s-rdd2022es-balanced40-best-single-v1. Its manifest records 832-pixel inference, minimum detection confidence 0.20 and area_quarter primary ranking. That inference threshold differs from the workflow's 0.60 raw-confidence gate for automatic task creation.

The committed single_damage_summary.json records 377 confirmation images (171 positive, 206 negative), with TP=106, FP=66, FN=65. Image-type precision is 61.63%, recall 61.99%, and eight-class macro F1 46.15%. These are primary-label image-type measures; they are not box-IoU localization or mAP metrics. The source separately records localization thresholds and multi-object evaluation.

This confirmation subset came from validation data already used for training/selection; it is not an independent held-out Jurong field test. Both typed precision and recall remain below the project's 70% targets. A confidence of 0.60 is not a measured 60% correctness probability, and passing software tests does not establish recognition accuracy or calibration. Source data does not prove Singapore/Jurong image provenance.

Sources: [src-model-manifest](../../model/releases/roadguard-single-v1.json), [src-vision-evaluation](../../experiments/vision/single_damage_summary.json), [src-workflow-service](../roadguard/inspections/service.py).

## Priority-first objective and metric meanings

classification: `demo_assumption`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-objective`.

The shared `b-objective-v1` evaluator minimizes the lexicographic tuple
`(unassigned_P1, unassigned_P2, unassigned_P3, J)`.
Earlier components take precedence: a lower scalar cost cannot compensate for leaving an extra P1 unassigned.

`J = 1.0 * makespan_minutes + 0.2 * total_travel_minutes + 0.5 * workload_std_minutes + 0.5 * priority_weighted_completion_minutes`.
Priority completion weights are P1=3, P2=2, P3=1. This is a demonstration weighted time objective, not monetary cost, distance, an accuracy score or solely travel time.

Makespan is the latest crew finish; return travel counts when enabled. Total travel includes depot legs. Workload standard deviation uses available crews' travel plus service, includes idle available crews at zero, and excludes unavailable crews. Priority-weighted completion is the weighted mean of assigned tasks' completion times relative to planning_start_at; it is not lateness. Lateness depends on due_at. When no assigned task has a deadline, lateness is null, not proven zero. Report assigned/unassigned counts and their priorities before scalar objective comparisons.

Sources: [src-routing-config](../../config/routing.example.json), [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py), [src-routing-models](../roadguard/routing/models.py).

## When GA and Greedy percentages are meaningful

classification: `confirmed_project_fact`. citation_id: `rg-kb-plans#plans-comparison`.

The frontend requires both complete plans and evidence from the same recalculation response. Matching algorithm labels or two latest-plan responses alone does not establish that the matrix was shared. Check plan IDs, input revision, start time, settings, depot, crews/availability, task set, task source, matrix provider/simulation flag and counts against that response. Duplicate tasks or inconsistent totals invalidate comparison.

Check the assigned task IDs as well as assigned counts. Comparisons of time metrics for equivalent work require the same assigned set. If coverage differs, report unassigned P1/P2/P3 and explain the difference before interpreting the objective; do not advertise a time saving caused by omitting work. Historical before/after plans with changed inputs can describe an operational change but cannot isolate the algorithm's effect.

For a comparable nonzero Greedy baseline, the frontend displays signed change `(GA - Greedy) / Greedy * 100`; negative means a reduction. If phrased as improvement, explicitly use `(Greedy - GA) / Greedy * 100` for a lower-is-better metric. Null values or a zero baseline have no percentage. Label the metric and units: durations/objective in minutes, algorithm_runtime_ms in milliseconds. Algorithm runtime is not travel time or end-to-end API latency.

Sources: [src-plan-comparison](../../frontend/src/planning/comparison.ts), [src-routing-models](../roadguard/routing/models.py), [src-routing-service](../roadguard/routing/service.py), [src-routing-evaluation](../roadguard/routing/evaluation.py).

## Current demo configuration

classification: `demo_assumption`. citation_id: `rg-kb-routing#routing-demo-settings`.

Configuration `b-routing-demo-v1` uses return_to_depot=true and a limited 480-minute shift per crew, including travel and service. An explicit unlimited shift is a different experiment. The shared project configuration still has return_to_depot=null/pending confirmation; the executable routing demo selects true independently and does not convert null to false. These choices and the objective weights are not approved operational policy.

The default `simulated_haversine_v1` matrix estimates great-circle distance times a 1.3 detour factor at 30 km/h, rounded to one decimal minute. Optional Google Routes uses DRIVE and TRAFFIC_UNAWARE. It supplies travel estimates, not verified road permission or a live-traffic guarantee. A Google failure reports an error and saves no plans; it does not silently switch to simulation. Routes currently have geometry=null; displayed straight lines are schematic.

Optional Google matrices and saved Google experiments exist; they do not establish road-work permission or current traffic.

due_at=null means no defined task deadline; the shared project return_to_depot=null means no defined operational return policy, while the routing demo explicitly selects true. Unknown duration is not zero, no available plan is not a valid empty plan, and unreachable travel is not zero minutes.
